hook: Selma had a museum. *Harlem's fight didn't.*
dek: The National Urban League opened the Urban Civil Rights Museum in Harlem, the first of its kind in New York City.
title: The Civil Rights Movement Happened Up North Too. Harlem Finally Has the Museum to Prove It.
yt_title: Urban Civil Rights Museum Harlem: What to Know

slides.label: The gap
slides.text: We learned civil rights as a *Southern* story. The fight in *Harlem, Chicago and Detroit* rarely got its own building.

slides.label: Now open
slides.text: The *National Urban League* opened the *Urban Civil Rights Museum* in Harlem, the first of its kind in NYC.

slides.label: Inside
slides.text: About *12,000 square feet*: the slave trade, both waves of the *Great Migration* and the movement's impact today.

slides.label: Your turn
slides.text: Feedback walls ask if you've ever *joined a protest* or *read a banned book*. The goal: for people "to see themselves."

slides.label: Harlem day
slides.text: Then walk to the *Schomburg Center's* free exhibition on *Arturo Schomburg*, on view through *Dec 5*.

question: Whose story belongs on these walls?
